To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the ischemic lesions were detected in the neuronal structure of the cerebral cortex and the caudopatamen after 7 minutes or 30 minutes of occlusion of the MCA, respectively.
the ischemic lesion is most prominent in the frontoputamen and that the lesion is reversible in the frontoparital cortex but not in the caudate nucleus.
the ischemic lesion of the cerebral cortex is characterized by a laminar loss and that the postischemia lesion of the caudopatamen is characterized by a diffuse lesion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the investigation of the progression and the recovery of ischemic lesions after middle cerebral artery ligation in the gerbil.
the development of a new model of cerebral ischemia and the immunohistochemistry of the gerbil brain after occlusion and reperfusion of the middle cerebral aery.

the development of immunohistochemical methods for the investigation of ischemia and the development of a new experimental model of cerebral ischemia in gerbils, which is suitable for investigation in the early stage of ischemia.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the gerbil is a useful model to investigate rapidly progressive ischemia in the frontoparital cortex and caudate nucleus, and that the model is useful to study reperfusion damage.
the gerbil is an excellent animal model for investigation of the pathogenesis and therapy of cerebral ischemia.
the gerbil is a good model for studying the pathophysiological and pharmacological effects of cerebral ischemia in humans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the ischemic lesions in neuronal structure and reactive astrocytes are detectable in the cerebral cortex after 10 minutes of ischemia and in the caudoptuminal area after 30 minutes and that the lesions in the neuronal structures and reactive astrocyte disappear after 24 hours in the cerebral cortex even after 15 minutes of ischemia, while the lesion in the cauodputamen disappear after 24 hour even after 30 minutes.

the ischemic lesion in the neuronal structure is more severe in the frontoposterior cerebral cortex than in the caudodorsal cerebral cortex, and that the ischemic and post-ischemic lesions in the caudate-putamen are more severe than in the cerebral cortex.

in gerbils the ischemia of 10 minutes or more in the cerebral cortex causes a neuronal damage which can be identified by the loss of tubulin immunoreactivity, and the ischemia of more than 15 minutes in caudoputaman causes a neuronal damage that can be identified by loss of the tubulin immunoreactive neurons.

we have a model for studying the pathophysiological mechanisms of cerebral ischemia and the effects of neuroprotective drugs.
the model is suitable for the investigation of rapidly progressive ischemic damage in the cerebral cortex.
